title: 逻辑电平 MOSFET：3.3 V 引脚开关大电流电机
summary: 先用普通的 IRF540N：3.3 V 栅压只让它半开，电机几乎不动。换成逻辑电平的 IRLZ44N，它全开，0.6 A 的电机转起来，自己几乎不发热。
concepts: N 沟道 MOSFET 低边开关 low-side switch
工作区对照 BJT / MOSFET regions
description: 直流开关：GPIO → 100 Ω → MOSFET 栅极（100 kΩ 下拉到 GND），电机和续流二极管接在 5 V 稳压电源和漏极之间。比较 IRF540N（Vth ≈ 3 V，3.3 V 栅压下只半开）和逻辑电平的 IRLZ44N（全开，Rds ≈ 43 mΩ），并对照三极管和 MOSFET 的工作区名称。PWM 调速在 5.8。

cards.title: 先用一颗“普通” MOSFET
text: **稳压电源**调到 **`5 V`**，限流调到 **`1 A`**，它的 − 接开发板 GND（**共地**）。
栅极这一串：GPIO → **`100 Ω`** → Q1 栅极 G；**`100 kΩ`** 从 G 接到 GND；Q1 的源极 S 接 GND。电机接在 +5 V 和漏极 D 之间，电机两端反并一个二极管（色环朝 +5 V）。
Q1 先用 **IRF540N**。把 GPIO 设成**「输出 高」**：电机转得起来吗？单击 Q1，看它在哪个区、自己发热多少。

cards.title: Vth 只是“开始导通”
text: - MOSFET 的栅极像电容的一块极板：**直流下不取电流**。栅压越高，D–S 之间的通道开得越大。
- 数据手册上的 **Vth** 是“刚刚开始导通”的栅压（只有零点几毫安）。IRF540N 的 Vth 约 3 V，3.3 V 只比它高一点，通道只开了一小半。**逻辑电平** MOSFET（IRLZ44N）的 Vth 约 1.5 V，3.3 V 足够让它全开。
![](fig:gate)
- 名字容易搞反：MOSFET 的“饱和区”是**半开**，三极管的“饱和区”才是**全开**。
| | NPN 三极管 | MOSFET |
| 关断 | 截止区 | 截止区 |
| 半开（受控的电流源） | 放大区 | **饱和区** |
| 全开（当开关用） | **饱和区** | **可变电阻区** |
- 全开时 D–S 就是一个很小的电阻 $R_{DS(on)}$，上面的电压很小：
$$V_{DS} = I_D × R_{DS(on)}$$
- 代入数字：本模拟器取 IRLZ44N 在 5 V 栅压下 22 mΩ（数据手册给的上限是 25 mΩ），1 A 时 $V_{DS} = 1 × 0.022 = 0.022$ V，自己几乎不发热。

cards.title: 换成逻辑电平 MOSFET
text: - 单击 **Q1**，在「属性」里把型号换成 **IRLZ44N**。再看它的工作区和电机。
- 点**「检查我的电路」**。通过后用电流表、万用表完成测量题；有一题要把型号**临时换回 IRF540N**。
- 先预测：电机约 8 Ω，接在 5 V 上要多大电流？全开的 Q1 上会剩多少电压？

cards.title: 带走
text: - **3.3 V 单片机要选逻辑电平 MOSFET**：看数据手册里 $R_{DS(on)}$ 是在多大栅压下规定的（要有 2.5 V 或 4.5 V 的值）。IRLZ44N、AO3400、Si2302 都可以。
- 当开关用的 MOSFET 要在**可变电阻区**，不是“饱和区”。
- **栅极下拉**（10–100 kΩ）一定要加：上电、复位时 GPIO 是输入，栅极悬空会让电机突然转起来。
- 真实电路里的坑：电机电流从单独的电源出，别从 USB 取；电源和开发板一定要**共地**。电机两端那个反并的二极管，下一个实验讲它为什么救命。

caption.text: 栅压从 0 往上加：IRLZ44N 过了 1.5 V 很快就全开；IRF540N 要到 3 V 才开始导通，GPIO 的 3.3 V 只让它开了一小半。

i18n.en: Raising the gate voltage from 0: the IRLZ44N is fully on soon after 1.5 V; the IRF540N only starts at 3 V, and the GPIO's 3.3 V opens it only a little.

label.text: 电机电流（占全开的比例）

en.startNote: **Half-built**: the ESP32, the 5 V motor supply (bottom rails), both ground jumpers, the motor and its flyback diode are wired. **Why**: the load and supply are repeated skills; the MOSFET gate drive is the lesson. **Your job**: place the IRLZ44N (c21: G, D, S), add RG (100Ω, GPIO4 → gate) and RPD (100kΩ, gate → GND), and tie the source to GND.
en.title: Logic-level MOSFET: a 3.3 V pin switches a high-current motor
en.summary: First an ordinary IRF540N: 3.3 V on the gate opens it only halfway and the motor barely moves. Swap in a logic-level IRLZ44N: fully on, the 0.6 A motor runs and the MOSFET hardly warms up.
en.description: A DC switch: GPIO → 100 Ω → MOSFET gate (100 kΩ pull-down to GND); the motor and a flyback diode sit between a 5 V bench supply and the drain. Compare the IRF540N (Vth ≈ 3 V, only half open at a 3.3 V gate) with the logic-level IRLZ44N (fully on, Rds ≈ 43 mΩ), and line up the transistor's and the MOSFET's region names. PWM speed control is in 5.8.

cards.title: First, an "ordinary" MOSFET
text: Set the **bench supply** to **`5 V`** with a **`1 A`** current limit, and wire its − to the board's GND (**common ground**).
The gate chain: GPIO → **`100 Ω`** → Q1's gate G; **`100 kΩ`** from G to GND; Q1's source S to GND. The motor goes between +5 V and the drain D, with a reversed diode across it (band towards +5 V).
Use an **IRF540N** for Q1 first. Set the GPIO to **Output HIGH**: does the motor get going? Click Q1 and look at its region and how much it heats itself.

cards.title: Vth only means "starting to conduct"
text: - A MOSFET's gate is like one plate of a capacitor: **it takes no DC current**. The higher the gate voltage, the wider the channel between D and S opens.

- The datasheet's **Vth** is the gate voltage where it *just starts* to conduct (a fraction of a milliamp). The IRF540N's Vth is about 3 V, so 3.3 V opens its channel only a little. A **logic-level** MOSFET (IRLZ44N) has Vth ≈ 1.5 V, and 3.3 V turns it fully on.
![](fig:gate)
- The names are easy to mix up: a MOSFET's "saturation" is **half open**; a transistor's "saturation" is **fully on**.
| | NPN transistor | MOSFET |
| off | cutoff | cutoff |
| half open (a controlled current source) | active | **saturation** |
| fully on (as a switch) | **saturation** | **ohmic** |
- Fully on, D–S is just a small resistance $R_{DS(on)}$, with very little voltage across it:
$$V_{DS} = I_D × R_{DS(on)}$$
- With numbers: this simulator gives the IRLZ44N 22 mΩ at a 5 V gate (the datasheet's maximum is 25 mΩ); at 1 A, $V_{DS} = 1 × 0.022 = 0.022$ V, so it hardly heats up.

cards.title: Swap in a logic-level MOSFET
text: - Click **Q1** and change its model to **IRLZ44N** in Properties. Look at its region and the motor again.
- Press **Check my circuit**. Once it passes, answer the questions with the ammeter and multimeter; one of them has you switch the model **back to IRF540N for a moment**.
- Predict first: the motor is about 8 Ω; how much current does it take from 5 V? How much voltage is left across a fully-on Q1?

cards.title: Take away
text: - **A 3.3 V microcontroller needs a logic-level MOSFET**: check the gate voltage the datasheet specifies $R_{DS(on)}$ at (it should list 2.5 V or 4.5 V). IRLZ44N, AO3400 and Si2302 all work.
- A MOSFET used as a switch should be in the **ohmic** region, not "saturation".
- Always add a **gate pull-down** (10–100 kΩ): at power-up and reset the GPIO is an input, and a floating gate can start the motor by itself.

- A real-world catch: take the motor current from its own supply, not USB, and always **share the ground** with the board. The reversed diode across the motor — the next lab shows why it saves the transistor.

compare: - IRLZ44N, Output HIGH: Vgs ≈ 3.29 V, ohmic, Id ≈ **0.62 A**, Vds ≈ **27 mV**, Rds ≈ 43 mΩ; Q1 dissipates only about 17 mW.
- IRF540N, Output HIGH: saturation (half open), Id ≈ 0.14 A, Vds ≈ **3.9 V**; Q1 dissipates about 0.54 W and the motor gets under a quarter of the current.
- Pin as input: the pull-down holds the gate at 0 V, motor stopped.
**Model note**: the motor is 8 Ω + 2 mH with no back EMF; the MOSFET is a piecewise square-law model Id = min(K·Vov·Vds, K·Vov²/2), with no gate capacitance or switching losses.

measurements.ask: Output HIGH: the motor current (ammeter between +5 V and the motor)
measurements.explain: About 8 Ω on 5 V: ≈ 0.62 A, 30 times what a GPIO can give.

measurements.ask: Output HIGH: Vds (red lead on D, black on S)
From your two readings, the on-resistance Rds = Vds / Id
measurements.explain: ≈ 43 mΩ: the model's 22 mΩ is at a 5 V gate; with 3.3 V on the gate it roughly doubles. Q1 dissipates only about 17 mW.

measurements.ask: Switch Q1 back to an IRF540N for a moment (still 3.3 V on the gate): Vds
measurements.explain: Vth ≈ 3 V is only a little below 3.3 V: it sits in "saturation" (half open), Id ≈ 0.14 A, Vds ≈ 3.9 V, dissipating 0.54 W itself.

measurements.ask: Set the GPIO to Input (as at the moment of power-up or reset). The motor:
choices: stays still: the 100 kΩ pull-down holds the gate at 0 V
starts: the gate floats and may be pulled up by noise
stays still: a MOSFET is fully on with no gate voltage
measurements.explain: An input pin drives nothing, so the gate only sees 100 kΩ to GND: 0 V, Q1 off. Without the pull-down the gate floats, and in a real circuit the motor may start by itself.

hints: Gate chain: GPIO → 100 Ω → G, plus 100 kΩ from G to GND. S to GND.
Motor between +5 V and D; diode across the motor with its band (cathode) on +5 V.
Set the bench supply to 5 V with a 1 A limit and wire its − to the board's GND.
tests: Output HIGH: motor runs, Q1 fully on (ohmic)
Output LOW: Q1 off, motor stopped
Pin as input (reset): the pull-down keeps the gate at 0 V, motor stopped
IRF540N instead: stuck in saturation (half open), little current

tests.name: 「输出 高」：电机转，Q1 全开（可变电阻区）
「输出 低」：Q1 截止，电机停
引脚是输入（复位时）：下拉让栅极保持 0 V，电机停
换成 IRF540N：停在饱和区（半开），电流很小

compare: - IRLZ44N，「输出 高」：Vgs ≈ 3.29 V，可变电阻区，Id ≈ **0.62 A**，Vds ≈ **27 mV**，Rds ≈ 43 mΩ，Q1 只发热约 17 mW。
- IRF540N，「输出 高」：饱和区（半开），Id ≈ 0.14 A，Vds ≈ **3.9 V**，Q1 自己发热约 0.54 W，电机只拿到不到四分之一的电流。
- 引脚是输入：下拉把栅极拉到 0 V，电机停。
**模型说明**：电机是 8 Ω + 2 mH，没有反电动势；MOSFET 是分段的平方律模型 Id = min(K·Vov·Vds, K·Vov²/2)，没有栅极电容和开关损耗。

measurements.ask: 「输出 高」：电机电流（电流表串在 +5 V 和电机之间）
measurements.explain: 电机约 8 Ω 接 5 V：≈ 0.62 A——GPIO 能给的 30 倍。

measurements.ask: 「输出 高」：Vds（红表笔接 D，黑表笔接 S）
measurements.explain: 完全导通（可变电阻区），Vds ≈ 27 mV。

measurements.ask: 用你的两个读数算导通电阻 Rds = Vds / Id
measurements.explain: ≈ 43 mΩ：模型的 22 mΩ 是栅压 5 V 时的值，3.3 V 栅压时大约翻倍。Q1 只发热约 17 mW。

measurements.ask: 把 Q1 临时换回 IRF540N（栅极仍是 3.3 V）：Vds
measurements.explain: Vth ≈ 3 V，只比 3.3 V 低一点：它停在“饱和区”（半开），Id ≈ 0.14 A，Vds ≈ 3.9 V，自己发热 0.54 W。

measurements.ask: 把 GPIO 设成「输入」（就像上电、复位的那一瞬间），电机会？
choices: 停着：100 kΩ 下拉把栅极拉到 0 V
转起来：栅极悬空，可能被干扰抬高
停着：MOSFET 没有栅极电压也是全开的
measurements.explain: 引脚是输入时什么都不驱动，栅极只靠 100 kΩ 接到 GND，所以是 0 V，Q1 截止。没有下拉，栅极悬空，真实电路里电机可能自己转起来。

hints: 栅极这一串：GPIO → 100 Ω → G，再加一个 100 kΩ 从 G 接到 GND。S 接 GND。
电机接在 +5 V 和 D 之间；二极管并在电机两端，色环（负极）朝 +5 V。
稳压电源调到 5 V、限流 1 A，它的 − 接开发板 GND。
startNote: **半成品**：ESP32、5 V 电机电源（下方轨道）、两组地线、电机和续流二极管都已接好。**为什么**：负载和电源是重复技能；这里要学的是 MOSFET 的栅极驱动。**你要做**：放 IRLZ44N（c21：G、D、S），加 RG（100Ω，GPIO4 → 栅极）、RPD（100kΩ，栅极 → GND），再把源极接 GND。
